Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10643 at 20 FR 8359 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed November 7, 1955; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the November 9, 1955 issue. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 638 to 3187 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence (the sentence barring changes in conditions). Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Albany Port District Railroad and other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees, designated in lists A and C attached to the order, and certain of their employees represented by the cooperating (non-operating) railway labor organizations designated in lists B and D attached to the order, on wage demands and on demands for changes in health and welfare agreements. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Albany Port District Railroad and other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10643 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10643_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10643_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_84f930ce02.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated December 12, 1955; the board states that, upon stipulation of the parties, the President extended the time for filing the report to December 12, 1955. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking December 12, 1955 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on December 12, 1955 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to January 11, 1956 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event.
